item.title: Poland, Ukraine accuse Russia of ‘escalation’ after strikes near border

item.title: Baghdad confirms attack on Saudi pipeline came from Iraq
item.description:
Saudi Arabia shut down its vital East-West pipeline after multiple drone attacks, intensifying the pressure on Gulf energy exports. The pipeline had provided a workaround for Saudi crude, allowing the kingdom to bypass the Strait of Hormuz; its shuttering threatens the loss of 4% of the global oil supply, Reuters reported. Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis also seized Perim Island in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, threatening a second major shipping route through the Red Sea. Together, the disruptions could further squeeze oil exports, driving prices higher — the price of Brent crude surged above $109 a barrel last week. “With two critical maritime arteries simultaneously being choked , the world is facing an increasing constriction” of global energy flows, a consultant told The Washington Post. — Lauren Morganbesser

item.title: Six dead, 130 missing after Indonesian ferry capsizes in Java Sea
item.description:
Indonesia's National Search and / Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency, REUTERS A ferry carrying 243 people overturned due to severe weather in Indonesia’s Java Sea on Sunday. While over 107 people have been rescued, 130 remain missing and the bodies of six passengers have been found. item.title: BRICS leaders voice concern over Middle East, condemn unilateral sanctions at India summit
item.description:
Russia’s president landed in India for a BRICS summit that looks set to underline a broader reordering of global alliances. The talks in Delhi — also set to be attended by China’s leader — point to India’s attempt to balance ties with global powers: It has long sought to deepen relations with the US, but is unlikely to meet Washington’s demands to curb relations with Moscow and is reportedly set to propose a strategic economic dialogue with Beijing . They also come amid efforts by several smaller powers to hedge against an unpredictable US: Canada is strengthening ties with European and African nations , Qatar’s prime minister just visited China , and Vietnam’s leader is visiting Russia, France, the US, and Canada this month. — Prashant Rao

item.title: Former EPA Officials: Trump Is Letting Data Centers Make People Sick
item.description:
While tech oligarchs grandstand about the existential danger AI superintelligence poses to humanity, former Environmental Protection Agency officials say we should be worried about a more immediate threat to our health: the data centers that power those AI models. The former EPA researchers, now working with the nonprofit Environmental Protection Network, are warning in a new report that since January 2025, Donald Trump’s EPA has embarked on a systematic weakening of pollution safeguards, permitting processes, inspection norms, and other guardrails—at least 30 different actions—that could increase the health risks associated with the data center boom. There are currently about 3,000 data centers in the United States, and more than 1,500 new centers are in the planning stages. item.title: Fighting in Yemen intensifies, and Houthis launch more attacks on Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Twenty-five years after 9/11, the United States is again fighting a major war in the Middle East. Drop Site’s Ryan Grim and Murtaza Hussain speak with Vali Nasr, professor of international affairs and Middle East studies at Johns Hopkins SAIS and a former senior adviser in the Obama administration, and Rob Malley, a senior fellow at Yale’s Jackson School of Global Affairs, former U.S. special envoy for Iran, longtime Middle East peace negotiator, and head of the Middle East program at the International Crisis Group. The conversation covers Ansarallah’s advance in Yemen, the battle over the Strait of Hormuz, Iran and the US duel strategies of economic pressure, the future of U.S. military bases in the Gulf, the collapse of the JCPOA, Iran’s nuclear calculations, and whether Washington has learned the lessons of Iraq, Afghanistan and the broader post-9/11 wars. item.title: Court Rules Against Trump Order to Keep Costly Michigan Coal Plant Running
item.description:
The Department of Energy overstepped when it ordered an aging coal-fired power plant in Michigan to stay open past its planned retirement date last year, a federal court ruled on Friday. The J.H Campbell plant is one of seven fossil fuel plants around the country that the Trump administration has forced to stay in operation, despite the pollution they cause and the enormous costs of keeping them online. Just before it was about to close last May, Trump’s Energy Department invoked short-term emergency powers under the Federal Power Act to keep the 64-year-old plant running, arguing that the threat of outages, along with the need for more energy to power data centers, constituted an emergency. item.title: Swedes vote in election that could see far-right in government
item.description:
As Sweden heads into a closely fought election, the far right is gaining ground by tapping into concerns over crime and security, issues that some voters increasingly associate with migration. On FRANCE 24, Stockholm University sociologist Zeth Isaksson said the movement has also softened its image in recent years, making it more acceptable to a broader electorate, while also cautioning against overstating the strength of the far right in Sweden.
